Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

**Possible root cause found: `session_id` header triggers 500**

Identified a specific trigger for these 500s on the opencode-go API. The `session_id` HTTP header — sent when a client enables session affinity — causes the opencode-go backend to return HTTP 500.

Tested against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`:
- Requests **without** the `session_id` header → **200** (even with thinking + stream + cache retention params)
- Requests **with** the `session_id` header → **500** (even with a minimal body of just model, messages, max_tokens)

The `x-client-request-id` and `x-session-affinity` headers alone do not trigger the error — only `session_id` does.

This would explain the "intermittent" pattern: clients that send session affinity headers via compat flags (like `sendSessionAffinityHeaders: true`) hit the 500, while those that do not succeed normally. The fix would be on the opencode-go API side to ignore or gracefully handle the `session_id` header rather than returning a server error.

Not a substitute for native retention (+1 for that), but until it lands, a possibly useful stopgap: I built showagent, an MIT-licensed TUI that lists every OpenCode session with its workspace and first/last messages, so you can actually see what's taking space and delete interactively (two-press confirm). It goes through your own `opencode` CLI (`opencode db` / session delete) rather than touching opencode.db directly, so it stays safe across schema changes. It also covers Claude Code/Codex/Gemini stores if you run several agents. Disclosure: I'm the author.

Looks like this fix does not cover worktrees scenario. I have a large project with a bunch of worktrees, and starting opencode from any worktree hangs the terminal with no response
After doing researching and checking logs, the issue was due to `git add --all`. Then I discovered this PR that addresses it, the fix is live, and my version is up to date.

This is models output after describing the issue and pointing to this PR:
```
The fix is a one-line change at line 229 of packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts:
- Current (broken for worktrees): const sourceIndex = path.join(source, "index") — source comes from --git-common-dir, so it always points to the main repo's .git/index
- Fixed: Run git rev-parse --git-path index with cwd: state.worktree, which resolves to the correct worktree-specific index path (e.g. .git/worktrees/<name>/index), falling back to the old behavior if it fails
```
Looking at PR changes the proposed fix makes sense.
And indeed if opencode is started from main repo there is no problem.
Please let me know if this rather be submitted as another ticket.

Adding one concrete downstream use case in support of this issue and PR #16513.

`quota-axi` is a small read-only quota reporter used by agents before they decide whether to start expensive work. For OpenCode Go, the useful integration point is exactly a machine-readable endpoint keyed by the existing Go API key, not a dashboard scrape or browser cookie flow.

The ideal response for agent routing would include the same three windows the dashboard already computes:

- rolling or 5 hour usage percent plus reset time
- weekly usage percent plus reset time
- monthly usage percent plus reset time
- optional spent and limit values in USD, if available from the same server-side counters

Two constraints matter for agent tooling:

- read-only: checking quota should not create model usage or mutate provider state
- cookie-free: API key auth lets CLIs, status bars, and automation avoid browser-cookie import

The proposed `/zen/go/v1/usage` shape in #16513 looks like the right direction because it reads `LiteTable` usage counters and uses the same `Subscription.analyze*Usage` logic as the workspace dashboard.

I think the important distinction here is that this is not just an "agent got confused" bug, it's an economic-boundary bug.

Once the runtime sees the same tool family producing the same outcome fingerprint repeatedly (in this case: `resource_list` -> empty/no-match -> reformulated prefix -> empty/no-match), that should stop counting as exploration and start counting as failed state transition.

A few controls that would have helped a lot here:

- track `tool + normalized intent + outcome fingerprint`, not just raw tool count
- break after N consecutive no-delta outcomes, even if the query string changes slightly
- record `last_meaningful_delta_at` so the runtime can tell the difference between real progress and search churn
- enforce a per-tool economic cap before the workspace-level spend cap gets touched
- emit a typed stop reason like `resource_search_exhausted` or `circuit_breaker_repeated_empty_result`

The part that stands out to me is the 277-call stretch. By that point the system has already proven it doesn't know something new; it's just burning budget while preserving the illusion of activity.

We've been caring about exactly this false-progress / runaway-spend class in MartinLoop, so I was glad to see this written up this concretely. If you're open to it, I'd genuinely value your feedback on whether the right abstraction here is "loop detection" or something stricter like "economic stop conditions around repeated no-delta agent behavior."
